headline: Antonelli keeps a cool head through a disrupted race in Monte Carlo
standfirst: Kimi Antonelli won the Monaco Grand Prix for Mercedes, finishing 6.271s ahead of Lewis Hamilton, with Isack Hadjar completing the podium after 78 laps of Monte Carlo.

sections.title: The start
sections.body: Kimi Antonelli lined up first on the grid. Antonelli converted that into the lead at the end of lap one. The biggest winner of the opening lap was Alonso, up 4 places to 17th.

sections.title: How it unfolded
sections.body: Antonelli was never headed, leading all 78 laps. The race was neutralised by 1 red flag (lap 68) and 2 safety car periods (lap 60–66, 66–68).

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body: Antonelli made 3 stops, running medium → hard → soft tyres. The field made 70 pit stops in total; the quickest stationary time was 2.1s for Hamilton on lap 28.

sections.title: Movers
sections.body: Fernando Alonso made up the most ground, climbing 11 places from 21st to 10th. Russell went the other way, slipping from 6th to 12th. Timing recorded 132 on-track position changes, 12 of them by Lindblad.

sections.title: Retirements
sections.body: Sainz (lap 71), Norris (lap 44), Verstappen (lap 1), Leclerc (lap 65), Stroll (lap 57), Bottas (lap 16) and Bearman (lap 28) failed to finish.

sections.title: Conditions and pace
sections.body: It stayed dry throughout. Track temperature ranged from 32°C to 44°C, with air at 23–25°C. Kimi Antonelli set the fastest lap, a 1:13.481 on lap 76.
